summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to grow ZnO films at low temperatures for cross-bar memory applications. The films were grown using various organic zinc precursors and oxygen precursors, with the aim of achieving controlled electrical properties, including both n-type and p-type characteristics. The low-temperature growth process enabled the production of ZnO films with reduced defect concentrations and improved electrical properties suitable for memory devices.
evidence: Properties of ZnO films grown by atomic layer deposition at low temperature are described. By selecting appropriate precursors and their pulses we obtained films with controlled electrical properties – from heavily n-type to p-type. Parameters of constructed Schottky and p–n junction are good enough for their application in a new generation of memory devices with cross-bar architecture.
